experiment: CPU-only constrained SMS spam classification with LoRA

dataset.name: SMS Spam Collection
dataset.citation: Almeida, T. & Hidalgo, J. (2011). SMS Spam Collection. UCI Machine Learning Repository. DOI:10.24432/C5CC84

deduplication.method: NFKC/lowercase/punctuation/digit/URL/email normalized exact templates; >=10-word templates also grouped by word-trigram Jaccard, transitive connected components; conflicting groups removed; one representative retained before splitting.

dataset.truncation_policy: Only long message content is truncated from the right to fit the configured prompt length; chat template and instruction remain complete.

classifier.scoring: argmax of two next-token label logits; probabilities normalized over labels only
classifier.training_objective: binary cross entropy through the two label logits, balanced sampler with equal class counts per training batch

selection.criterion: highest validation macro F1, then lowest validation binary-label loss; baseline included

naive_bayes.method: Multinomial Naive Bayes, normalized word counts, training-only vocabulary and class priors; unseen vocabulary ignored
naive_bayes.selection: highest validation macro F1; ties keep first declared alpha

naive_bayes_matched_selected_training_ro.method: Multinomial Naive Bayes, normalized word counts, training-only vocabulary and class priors; unseen vocabulary ignored
naive_bayes_matched_selected_training_ro.selection: highest validation macro F1; ties keep first declared alpha

classical_baselines.matched_baseline_policy: Train on the unique rows seen up to the validation-selected LoRA checkpoint; select smoothing on the same validation set. Null if the untrained checkpoint is selected.

limitations: Historical public SMS dataset, not a current production spam filter.
Pretrained-model contamination cannot be ruled out; the dataset predates the base model.
Template and near-duplicate grouping is heuristic, not sender/source disjointness.
This is discriminative two-label classification, not unrestricted generation accuracy.
Training uses a balanced sampler; reported probabilities are not calibrated deployment spam probabilities.
Classical baseline sees all training rows, while LoRA sees the recorded fixed-budget sampled rows.
No guarantee these findings generalize to other tasks or language-model capabilities.
Sampled process RSS is not exact peak or total system memory.
